  Video super-resolution (VSR) involves restoring a clear high-resolution (HR)
video from a low-resolution (LR) counterpart. The recent progress of VSR has
been driven by video recurrent structures, which aggregate spatietemporal
information from the entire input clip through recurrent propagation. Among
different recurrent structures, BasicVSR has achieved the state-of-the-art
performance due to bidirectional propagation with feature alignment. In this
study, we delinate the effectiveness of recurrent structures for VSR and point
out the limitations of BasicVSR, specifically: (1) one-sided propagation and
(2) frame-wise alignment. To boost the performance of VSR, we propose to
augment BasicVSR with second-order grid propagation and flow-guided deformable
alignment. The new modules enable more efficient and accurate information
exploitation across misaligned frames via bidirectional propagation.
Specifically, we perform frame-wise propagation from neighboring frames and
grid propagation from all frames for intermediate feature aggregation.

meaningful improvements (0.82 dB in PSNR) over BasicVSR on various VSR
datasets, even without extra parameters. We also show that our method is
effective when incorporated into a transformer framework, which achieves 0.63
dB improvement in PSNR.

from training on multiple related tasks by exploiting similarities among them.
While such settings have been shown to benefit from experience reuse and
generalization, the question of whether the order of the taught tasks affects
the learning process has not been thoroughly investigated. We address this
question and show that even in a simple control multi-task learning scenario,
training the agent on one task before another can significantly impact the
learner. Most surprisingly, our experiments suggest that the beneficial effect
of the order of tasks can be of orders of magnitude in terms of the learned
performance, far beyond what can be achieved by simply combining the experiences
from the tasks. We also seek to explain the empirical observations and suggest
that the order of the tasks can be seen as a form of prior in a Bayesian
perspective. Building on this analogy, we propose a simple approach to encode
the learned information from one task as a prior for the next task, leading
to a significant performance boost. Our results further highlight the power of
relating different tasks in multi-task reinforcement learning and motivate
further investigations into handling transfer between tasks.
  We also study the question of how to optimally order the tasks and propose
a straightforward approach based on the expected performance gain from each
task. While the resulting orderings are empirically shown to be beneficial,
our experiments also suggest that the orderings are highly unpredictable and
further investigations into the task order are necessary.
  Finally, we study the influence of different exploration strategies and
observe that random noise is not the optimal parameter choice for multi-task
reinforcement learning. We argue that the optimal parameter depends on the
complexity of the task and the amount of experience gathered in the previous
tasks.
  In summary, our work shows that the order of the tasks can significantly
affect the multi-task reinforcement learning process and proposes strategies to
exploit the learned information from one task to the next.

  Eye-in-hand camera calibration is the process of continuously updating the
camera-flange transformation of a robot from a camera. We present a framework
that accelerates this process through classical camera calibration and machine
learning. First, we localise the camera on a new pose with a learning-based
detector, then we perform classical camera calibration on the predicted
location. We present several learning-based detectors for this purpose, including
edge-based and deep learning-based approaches. Furthermore, we show that
combining classical and learning-based camera calibration we can solve the
problem for several challenging scenarios, including low-texture and
translational motion.

computed tomography, deblurring, superresolution, inpainting, and other
applications. It is often the case that many image hypotheses are consistent
with both the measurements and prior information, and so the goal is not to
recover a single "best" hypothesis but rather to explore the space of probable
hypotheses, i.e., to sample from the posterior distribution. In this work, we
propose a regularized conditional Wasserstein GAN architecture that can
generate dozens of high-quality posterior samples per second. Using
architecture-specific training techniques, we obtain reliable samples after
less than 1 hour of training. We use our generator to train a classifier to
compare the quality of 10 different state-of-the-art MRI reconstruction
methods. We also demonstrate that our sampler can be used to predict
condition-specific reconstruction pathways. We validate our methodology with

interoperability, multi-access and flexibility are the key features of the
next generation networks and the spatial degrees of freedom (DOF) provided by
the THz communication systems can be leveraged to implement spatial
multiplexing, spatial diversity and multi-user spatial sharing such as spatial
multiplexing and spatial interference cancellation to achieve these features.
However, the THz signals are highly susceptible to the atmospheric
turbulence which can worsen the system performance especially when the
communication links are not guided. The pair-wise communications through the
guided channels, on the other hand, can provide stable links but the use of a
common channel for multiple users would not be able to leverage the spatial
degrees of freedom fully. To leverage the spatial DOF fully, multi-point
connections through the THz guided channels are needed. For this purpose, the
optical fiber based multi-point connections are traditionally leveraged by
placing an optical-fiber at the common channel. However, the optical-fiber can
cause signal attenuation and also limit the data rates due to the lower THz
generation and reception rates at the fiber-fiber interface compared to the
THz-THz direct connection. To address this problem, the simple conversion
schemes from the optical to THz and vice versa are not effective as the
additional components are needed for the conversions. In this paper, we
propose the multi-point THz connections through the THz guided channels without
the need of optical-fiber at the link ends. We leverage the phase change
phenomenon at the metal-gas and metal-vacuum interfaces to modulate the
propagation phase of the THz signals at the multi-exit junctions (MEJs). We
present and verify the system performance for the MEJs with and without the
atmospheric turbulence for the monolithic and discrete component implementations.
We show that the data rates of 100 Gbps and 1.2 Tbps are achieved with the bit
rates of 10 Gbps and 1.2 Gbps, respectively, for the proposed MEJs in the THz
frequency band.

resolving these scattering screens and a means of measuring their properties.
In this paper, we report our analysis of 34 years of Arecibo observations of
PSR B1133+16, from which we have obtained high-quality dynamic spectra and
their associated scintillation arcs, arising from the scattering screens
located along the line of sight to the pulsar. We have identified six
individual scattering screens that are responsible for the observed
scintillation arcs, which persist for decades. Using the assumption that the
scattering screens have not changed significantly in this time, we have modeled
the variations in arc curvature throughout the Earth's orbit and extracted
information about the placement, orientation, and velocity of five of the six
screens, with the highest-precision distance measurement placing a screen at
just $5.46^{+0.54}_{-0.59}$ pc from the Earth. We associate the more distant of
these screens with an under-dense region of the Local Bubble.
  We find that the density of the fifth screen is $1.38^{+0.23}_{-0.18} \times
10^{-3}$ particles cm$^{-3}$, and estimate that it contains at least $1.9 \times
10^{-7} M_{\odot}$ of gas. By assuming a typical heavy element abundance and
estimating the electron density, we calculate that this screen contains at least
$1.4 \times 10^{-7}$ $M_{\odot}$ of dust. Using its observed scattering
properties, we estimate that the screen interacts with the solar wind to
generate at least $1.3 \times 10^{-8} L_{\odot}$ of far-UV emission.
  Five of the six screens are found to be moving in the same direction as the
Local Bubble's inferred outflow velocity (~ 16.7 km/s). Three of these
screens are likely to be in the direction of the Lyman-alpha "density
plateaus" reported by Cox et al. (1993), which suggests that they are
associated with the known scattering screens that affect the Lyman-alpha
emission of the Sun. The motions of the scattering screens reported here
highlights the utility of pulsar scintillation for resolving the interstellar
medium and studying its dynamics.

Quasi-Periodic WaveNet (QPNet) is proposed to improve the limited pitch
controllability of vanilla WaveNet (WN) using pitch-dependent dilated
convolution neural networks (PDCNNs). Specifically, as a probabilistic
autoregressive generation model with stacked dilated convolution layers, WN
achieves high-fidelity audio waveform generation. However, the pure-data-driven
nature and the lack of prior knowledge of audio signals degrade the pitch
controllability of WN. For instance, it is difficult for WN to precisely
generate the periodic components of audio signals when the given auxiliary
fundamental frequency ($F_{0}$) features are outside the $F_{0}$ range observed
in the training data. To address this problem, QPNet with two novel designs is
proposed. First, the PDCNN component is applied to dynamically change the
network architecture of WN according to the given auxiliary $F_{0}$ features.
Second, a cascaded network structure is utilized to simultaneously model the
long- and short-term dependencies of quasi-periodic signals such as speech. The
performances of single-tone sinusoid and speech generations are evaluated. The
experimental results show the effectiveness of the PDCNNs for unseen auxiliary
$F_{0}$ features and the effectiveness of the cascaded structure for speech
generation.

extract the shape and color of the road markings. RoadAtlas is designed to be
cloud-native with a microservices architecture that allows for the development of
each service independently. Additionally, our system is highly scalable,
reliable, and available. We demonstrate our system with a set of experiments and

existing grading labels are limited to large lesion categories and do not
capture the detailed histological patterns that characterize different
adenomas grades.

classification and grading. We find that a model trained to distinguish

  We propose a novel off-policy correction for supervised learning. A
fundamental problem in supervised learning is that of optimizing the expected
loss over the training distribution. However, the expected loss often differs
from the observed loss, and standardizing to obtain expectations is not
possible. We formulate a framework for rewriting the expectation into a
sum, which allows us to use off-policy correction to minimize the bias. We
discuss the theoretical foundations, practical implementations, and connections
to recent works. Under certain conditions, our approach converges to
reinforcement learning (RL) following the maximum likelihood policy Grange and
Baptiste (2019); Menasché (2019), yet with much less sample complexity.
Notably, our framework can also be seen as providing explicit priors for RL.
We demonstrate the efficacy of our approach by reducing the bias of recent
state-of-the-art transformer models, which leads to improved empirical
performance.

2-D domains is a subject of great importance for the numerical solution of
Poisson's equation and volume integral equations. Complicated domains typically
require discretization by unstructured meshes, over which the direct evaluation
of the potential by quadrature becomes costly. In this paper, we present a
simple and efficient high-order algorithm for computing Newtonian potentials,
based on the use of Green's third identity for transforming the volume integral
into a collection of boundary integrals, which can be easily handled by the
Helsing-Ojala method. As a result, the time cost of the classically expensive
near field and self-interaction computations over an unstructured mesh becomes
roughly the same as the time cost of the FMM-based far field interaction
computation. One of the key components of our algorithm is the high-order 2-D
monomial approximation of a function over a mesh element, which is often
regarded as an ill-conditioned problem, since it involves the solution of a
Vandermonde linear system. In fact, it has long been observed that, when the
function is sufficiently smooth, and when a backward stable linear system
solver is used, the resulting monomial expansion can approximate the function
uniformly to high accuracy. We rigorously formalize this observation in this
paper. The performance of our algorithm is illustrated through several
numerical experiments.
  From a mathematical point of view, our work amounts to obtaining new bounds on
the classical degree of best approximation of a function by a monomial in two
variables. A interesting extension of our work would be to obtain similar
results for higher order potentials, such as the Laplace double layer, and to
study the convergence properties of the resulting schemes.
  Our algorithm for computing Newtonian potentials has been incorporated into a
volume integral equation solver for slowly moving drops, which is available
online at https://github.com/afgorman/slowDropletSolver. We would like to
